title: Aftershift clipboard: night summary, escalations & runbook deltas
content:
Context: quick clipboard for the on-call team after the 2026-08-31 23:40 UTC latency spike. This is a working doc — raw notes, open questions, and a short list of follow-ups. Save an editable copy into the SRE runbooks if we agree on the runbook deltas below.

Summary (TL;DR):
- 23:38 UTC: abrupt p95 token-generation latency increase observed on api-redwood-prod cluster (region-us-west1). Alert: latency-p95-high-fired (threshold 450ms).
- 23:40 UTC: increased error rate from 0.2% -> 3.5% for model-serving route /v1/generate (mostly 502/504).
- 23:42 UTC: traffic shifted to fallback model variants automatically per routing policy; partial mitigation but p95 still elevated.
- 00:05 UTC: root cause traced to a cascading cache eviction on shared kv-cache nodes causing severe disk IO on on-prem NFS tier (private customers still on older storage mix).
- 00:24 UTC: engineers throttled cache warm-up and enabled KV-prefetch backoff; p95 returned to baseline by 00:40 UTC.
- Impact: 55 minutes of elevated latency for ~7% of requests in us-west1; error spike impacted ~1.2% of total tokens served across the infra during window.

Chronology / quick timeline (notes to self style):
- 23:30–23:38: Routine infra deploy (infra-team) — low risk, rolling changes to autoscaler settings for dedicated pools (PR #281). No immediate signals.
- 23:38: Alert fires on latency-p95-high. Pager carried to on-call.
- 23:39: On-call (Aisha) opens incident channel, initial triage: check model CPU/GPU utilization, node-level swapping, and cache hit rates.
- 23:40: Observed sudden drop in cache hit-rate on kv-cache-usw1 (~cache hit 94% -> 61%). Simultaneous spike in NFS IO wait on two cache nodes (kv-node-07 and kv-node-09).
- 23:44: Error 502s originate in grpc proxy layer when cache lookup timeout exceeded and upstream model runtime also saw long tail.
- 23:47: Routed traffic to fallback model variants (smaller quantized models). Partial success; throughput preserved but latency remained high for large-context requests.
- 23:55: Infra noticed burst of small file reads on NFS (eviction-driven).
- 00:05: Decided to enable KV-prefetch backoff and reduce new cache population rate (safely throttled writer jobs).
- 00:24: Metrics show cache hit-rate recovering, NFS IO dropping.
- 00:40: p95 back to baseline; incident declared resolved at 00:50 after 3 full monitoring cycles.

Root cause hypothesis (short):
- A change in autoscaler/placement (PR #281) shifted cached shard leadership such that two previously quiet cache nodes received more load at once. The combination of cache-population traffic and a stale NFS inode cache warm-up caused an IO storm and excessive latency when cache lookups blocked.
- Contributing factor: no per-node write-rate cap on KV-populate worker and insufficient NFS IO qos configured for cache nodes in the private deployment profile.

Immediate mitigation we used:
- Traffic routing to smaller model variants (automatic fallback).
- KV-prefetch backoff toggle (manual) to slow population.
- Temporary increase in cache lookup timeout to avoid proxy-level 502s while allowing slow-but-successful responses to proceed.

Runbook deltas / draft edits (propose to PR into latency-playbook and runbooks ops folder):
1) Add a new section: "kv-cache node IO saturation"
   - Symptoms: sudden cache-hit drop, NFS IO wait climb, 502s in proxy.
   - Triage steps: check node-level iostat for high await (>40ms), check NFS server metrics (ops_nfs_io_wait), check shard leadership map and recent placement changes (git tag/PRs affecting placement).
   - Short mitigation: toggle kv-prefetch-backoff (ops flag), temporarily reduce cache-populate worker concurrency to 2 per node, and route long-context requests to fallback variants.
   - Owner: eng-serving-runtime + eng-infrastructure (add to runbook metadata).
2) Add a pre-deploy check for PRs that touch autoscaler / placement config: ensure auto-simulation of shard reassignments on staging with kv-cache workload.
3) Add per-node NFS IO QoS guardrail in Private deployment profile: throttle background population jobs if node-level await > 30ms.

Open questions / items that need design decisions:
- Should we fail fast and route to fallback models when cache hit-rate drops more than X% within Y minutes? (current routing is conservative)
- Do we want a hard write-rate cap for cache-populate workers globally or per-node? Global caps can cause cold-cache TTL regressions for high-traffic customers.
- How do we simulate NFS inode warm-up on staging? Need a test harness that mimics sustained small-file reads at scale.

Action items (short-term):
- Aisha: Draft the runbook changes above and open PR to Confluence + internal runbook repo by 2026-09-03. (in-progress)
- Evan: Add a gated pre-deploy hook to CI to detect placement changes and run a cheap shard-rebalance sim in staging; due 2026-09-10. (accept)
- María: Assess Private deployment NFS QoS settings and propose a QoS map by 2026-09-08. Focus on write/read limits for kv-cache nodes. (assigned)
- Liam: Investigate whether autoscaler PR #281 caused unbalanced shard leadership; produce an annotated diff and test plan by 2026-09-05. (assigned)
- Follow-up incident review meeting: propose 2026-09-07 16:00 UTC (30m) — invite eng-serving-runtime, infra, and product infra lead.

Longer-term / backlog (nice-to-have, not urgent):
- Implement per-tenant isolated cache shards for Private tier to limit cross-tenant eviction storms.
- Add synthetic workload to staging that exercises cold-start cache population under NFS-backed kv-store.
- Explore migrating caching layer to local SSD-backed nodes for private customers (requires procurement + migration plan).

Communication notes (what was said externally):
- Customer-facing: CS prepared a short note for impacted enterprise customers explaining a latency blip due to internal cache replenishment; no customer data was exposed. Drafted by CS on 2026-09-01 01:10 UTC.
- Internal: Incident channel summary posted in #sre-incidents, pinned.

Misc / scratchpad (notes to self):
- There are still some ~30ms tail spikes in model runtime for >16k token requests even after cache warmed — verify whether related to KV fetch blocking on large KV fetch sets.
- Check autoscaler logs on 2026-08-31 23:30–23:50 for any scale decisions that align with the spike.
- Revisit the proxy's 502 semantics: we raised timeout temporarily; consider a smarter backoff vs immediate 502 for cache misses.
- Reminder: sync with product-hosted-api on routing policy thresholds before changing failover behavior.

What to include in the post-incident doc:
- A brief timeline (cleaned) + metric charts (p95, cache hit-rate, NFS await), links to PR/changes.
- Root cause analysis (final) when we confirm autoscaler placement role.
- Concrete runbook edits (additions above) and owner signoffs.
- Postmortem with follow-ups and deadlines attached to Jira-INC-4821.

If you take anything from this doc: copy into the runbooks folder, add owners to the specific runbook bullets, and drop a quick note in #sre-incidents so we can lock the postmortem date.

Quick links referenced in above notes:
- PR/infra change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/281
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4821
- Slack incident thread: https://slack.com/archives/C01AB2XYZ/p1693550400000123

End of clipboard.

-- Aisha (on-call)
